**Blues Scale in the Key of A**

| Note | Interval from the previous note |
|------|---------------------------------|
| A    | —                               |
| C    | **+3** semitones (minor 3rd)    |
| D    | **+2** semitones (major 2nd)    |
| E♭   | **+1** semitone (minor 2nd)     |
| E    | **+1** semitone (minor 2nd)     |
| G    | **+3** semitones (major 3rd)    |
| A (octave) | **+2** semitones (major 2nd) |

**Pattern of intervals:**  
`+3, +2, +1, +1, +3, +2`

**In terms of scale degrees:**  
Root – minor 3rd – perfect 4th – diminished 5th (the “blue” note) – perfect 5th – minor 7th.

So the A‑blues scale consists of the notes **A, C, D, E♭, E, G** (and then back to A).
